article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Blueberry Muffin × Dream Queen
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Company
THC Content: 26–30%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet apple, floral fruit, blueberry, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 45 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early September
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Few modern cannabis strains reach harvest as quickly as Apple Blossom without behaving like an autoflower. Humboldt Seed Company created this photoperiod strain by bringing together Blueberry Muffin and Dream Queen, two of its best-known early-finishing cultivars, then selecting heavily for speed, production, resin, and an aroma that shifts from delicate flowers into freshly cut apple. The breeder lists only about 45 days of indoor flowering, putting the cultivar among the fastest photoperiod marijuana varieties in its catalog. Dense trichome-coated buds can develop blue and purple accents as they mature, creating an appearance that mirrors the fruit-and-flower character of the name.

The unusual part is that speed did not come at the expense of potency. THC can reach approximately 26–30%, while the effects retain a balanced-hybrid character rather than becoming excessively sedating. The first phase is typically uplifting, energetic, and mentally engaging; later, a warmer physical relaxation appears and appetite may increase. Combined with high production, substantial secondary branching, and a September outdoor finish, Apple Blossom occupies a useful middle ground between boutique flower and practical commercial cannabis genetics.
Genetics and Lineage

Apple Blossom is Blueberry Muffin × Dream Queen, and both parents contribute traits that can be recognized clearly in the offspring. Blueberry Muffin is Humboldt Seed Company’s Purple Panty Dropper × Razzleberry line, worked through multiple generations for consistency. Its contribution includes blueberry sweetness, baked or muffin-like aromatics, resin, purple coloration, and a rapid flowering schedule. Dream Queen approaches the cross from a more energetic direction, combining Green Crack , Mazar Star, and Skunk #1 into a vigorous sativa-dominant plant noted for enormous production, sweet pine, orange, Skunk, and a similarly short flowering period.

Bringing those parents together creates more than a simple fruit-on-fruit hybrid. Dream Queen supplies the growth engine: vigorous branching, substantial flower production, rapid maturation, and enough sativa influence to keep the high lively. Blueberry Muffin adds deeper fruit, floral sweetness, resin density, purple pigmentation, and a more relaxing second half. Their shared tendency toward fast flowering helps explain why the finished cultivar can mature in roughly 45 days rather than requiring the eight to ten weeks expected from many high-THC hybrids.

The extended family tree also explains the strain’s wide aromatic range. Purple Panty Dropper and Razzleberry sit behind the blueberry and floral side, while Green Crack, Mazar Star, and Skunk #1 introduce citrus, pine, herbal pungency, and vigor. Apple may be the headline aroma, but the genetics underneath it contain berry pastry, Skunk, citrus, pine, flowers, and earthy sweetness. That layered ancestry keeps the finished weed from tasting like a one-note apple-flavored novelty.
Effects and Experience

The high usually develops with momentum rather than heaviness. Mental energy rises first, often bringing a more positive mood, increased interest in conversation, and a stronger pull toward music, creative projects, or active recreation. Humboldt Seed Company characterizes the effect as uplifting and energizing, which is consistent with the Dream Queen influence. At moderate amounts, the experience can remain clear enough to feel functional, although the potency means concentration may become less reliable once the dose increases.

A different character appears later. Warmth can move through the body, muscular tension softens, and appetite may become considerably more noticeable. The transition is gradual rather than abrupt, allowing the strain to feel genuinely balanced instead of alternating between two disconnected effects. Consumers who use smaller quantities may stay closer to the bright cerebral side, while heavier consumption can expose more of the relaxing Blueberry Muffin influence and eventually make a quiet setting more appealing than activity.

THC in the 26–30% range deserves respect even when the experience begins cheerfully. High-potency cannabis can turn stimulation into anxiety, racing thoughts, dizziness, dry mouth, or short-term memory disruption if too much is consumed. Apple Blossom may therefore feel surprisingly strong to someone expecting a mild fruit strain. The balanced genetics make it versatile, but the potency makes dosage more important than the indica/sativa ratio alone.
Medical Benefits

An uplifting beginning followed by physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer avoiding immediate sedation. Some people choose cannabis with this general effect pattern when dealing with poor appetite, discomfort, tension, low mood, or difficulty relaxing later in the day. The breeder also associates the cultivar with increased hunger, which is consistent with the appetite stimulation some consumers experience as the initial energetic phase begins to settle.

Apple Blossom itself has not been tested in controlled clinical trials, so it should not be described as a proven treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, nausea, or another condition. Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly suggests potential usefulness for certain forms of chronic pain and nausea, but clinical effects depend on cannabinoid composition, dose, route of administration, and the individual patient. A high-THC flower cultivar is chemically different from standardized cannabinoid medicines used in medical research.

Its potency may also create problems for people who are particularly sensitive to THC. Anxiety, dizziness, cognitive impairment, and altered coordination can occur even when the desired effect is relaxation. Marijuana can also interact with some medications. Medical consumers should therefore use current laboratory results and cautious dosing rather than assuming that a pleasant apple aroma or balanced-hybrid classification makes the cultivar inherently gentle.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet apple provides the central theme, but it arrives with a surprisingly delicate floral quality rather than the intense artificial candy character found in some modern fruit strains. A freshly opened flower may suggest crisp apple flesh, blossoms, and mild sugary fruit before darker notes from the parental lines emerge. Blueberry Muffin can contribute berry pastry and soft herbal sweetness, while Dream Queen introduces citrus, pine, and a subtle Skunk edge that keeps the bouquet from becoming excessively sweet.

The flavor can resemble warm apple dessert without literally tasting like baked pie. Sweet apple and floral fruit appear early, followed by blueberry, citrus peel, mild herbs, and a slightly woody or pine-like finish. Some phenotypes may emphasize fruit almost completely, while others show more of the Dream Queen side and finish with noticeable Skunk or citrus. Purple-leaning plants can still share the same aromatic profile; pigmentation is not an indication that the flavor will automatically become darker or grape-like.

Humboldt Seed Company does not publish a permanent terpene percentage breakdown for Apple Blossom, so assigning one fixed dominant compound would be misleading. The breeder instead emphasizes the sensory profile, which is unusually consistent around floral sweetness and apple. Proper drying matters considerably because the lighter floral and fresh-fruit aromas are more volatile than pine, herbs, or Skunk. A slow, controlled cure gives the apple character a better chance to remain distinct in the finished flower.
Growing Information

Speed is the cultivar’s most obvious horticultural advantage. Humboldt Seed Company lists approximately 45 days of indoor flowering, an exceptionally short schedule for a high-potency feminized photoperiod strain. Plants are vigorous and produce numerous secondary branches, so growers can create a broad productive canopy without an excessively long vegetative period. The breeder also categorizes the strain as easy to cultivate and highly productive, making it approachable for newer growers while still offering the yield potential sought by more experienced cultivators.

Outdoor timing is equally useful. Harvest normally falls between September 15 and September 30, allowing mature cannabis to come down before the wettest and coldest portion of autumn in many Northern Hemisphere climates. Blueberry Muffin and Dream Queen are both early finishers, so that trait has a strong genetic foundation rather than being an isolated selection. Cooler nights can encourage blue and purple coloration in the flowers and surrounding leaves, while healthy plants continue developing dense trichome coverage through the final stage of maturation.

Humboldt lists indoor and outdoor production simply as high rather than attaching a universal weight to the strain. That is sensible because plant size, lighting, root volume, vegetative time, climate, nutrition, and training can dramatically change final yield. The naturally abundant branching responds well to canopy management, although crowding should be avoided because dense trichome-rich buds still require good airflow. Once harvested, a gradual dry is preferable to aggressive heat; preserving the floral apple aroma should take priority over shortening an already exceptionally fast production cycle.
FAQ
What is the genetics of Apple Blossom?

Apple Blossom was bred by Humboldt Seed Company from Blueberry Muffin × Dream Queen. Blueberry Muffin is Purple Panty Dropper × Razzleberry, while Dream Queen combines Green Crack, Mazar Star, and Skunk #1.
Is Apple Blossom indica or sativa?

The breeder classifies it as a balanced hybrid at approximately 50% indica and 50% sativa. Its effects reflect that balance, beginning with uplifting mental energy before gradually developing a more relaxing physical side.
How strong is Apple Blossom?

Humboldt Seed Company lists THC at approximately 26–30%, with current breeder information averaging around 27%. That places the cultivar firmly in high-potency territory despite its sweet floral flavor and relatively approachable effects.
What does Apple Blossom taste like?

Sweet apple and delicate floral notes lead the profile, followed by blueberry, citrus, mild pastry sweetness, pine, herbs, and occasional Skunk. The exact balance varies somewhat by phenotype and cure.
How long does Apple Blossom take to flower?

Indoor flowering takes approximately 45 days. Outdoors, Humboldt Seed Company places harvest between roughly September 15 and September 30, making it one of the breeder’s faster photoperiod cultivars.
Final Thoughts on Apple Blossom

Apple Blossom brings together two Humboldt Seed Company lines that already excel at rapid flowering and gives their strongest qualities a new direction. Blueberry Muffin supplies berry sweetness, resin, color, and a calmer physical side, while Dream Queen adds vigorous production, citrus and pine, Skunk influence, and an energetic mental character. The resulting Blueberry Muffin × Dream Queen cross feels balanced because neither parent disappears completely.

Cultivation may be the strain’s biggest practical advantage. A roughly 45-day indoor bloom is rare among potent photoperiod marijuana, and a September 15–30 outdoor harvest gives growers a substantial head start on autumn weather. High production, strong secondary branching, dense resinous flowers, and an easy-growing reputation make the plant useful in gardens where efficiency matters as much as flavor.

The sensory profile gives that efficiency personality. Sweet apple and delicate flowers lead into berry, citrus, pine, herbs, and mild Skunk, producing more complexity than the name alone implies. THC reaching roughly 26–30% adds considerable strength, yet the experience can remain bright and engaging before physical relaxation becomes more prominent.

Apple Blossom ultimately succeeds because its desirable traits reinforce rather than compete with one another. It flowers fast without behaving like an autoflower, produces heavily without sacrificing trichome coverage, and delivers high modern potency alongside a soft floral-fruit profile. For consumers, the appeal is sweet apple, euphoria, energy, and a relaxing finish; for growers, it is a high-yielding photoperiod cultivar capable of reaching harvest weeks earlier than many comparable hybrids.
